title: Affine fpqc coverings admit finite standard refinements
statement: Let $T=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $\{f_i:T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Then there are a finite set $J$, indices $a:J\to I$, and affine opens $V_j\subset T_{a(j)}$ such that each $V_j=\operatorname{Spec}(A_j)$ and the induced ring map $R\to\prod_{j\in J}A_j$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Definition Tag 022B (topologies-definition-fpqc-covering), together with the affine refinement used in Descent Lemma Tag 03N0

proof.text: Apply the defining affine-open condition of the fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] to $T$ itself. It gives a finite index set $J$, a map $a:J\to I$, and affine opens $V_j=\operatorname{Spec}(A_j)\subseteq T_{a(j)}$ whose images cover $T$. The definition also gives flatness of every $f_i$; the construction allows $J=\varnothing$ when $T=\varnothing$.

source.place: Definition Tag 022B (topologies-definition-fpqc-covering), affine-open condition with U = T

proof.text: For each $j$, apply the affine-chart flatness criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] to the flat morphism $f_{a(j)}:T_{a(j)}\to T$ and its affine open $V_j$. Thus the induced map $R=\mathcal O_T(T)\to\mathcal O_{T_{a(j)}}(V_j)=A_j$ is flat. The finite product $\prod_{j\in J}A_j$ is flat as an $R$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-product-flat-modules], so the product ring map is flat.

source.place: Lemma Tag 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize), clause (1) implies (2); finite-product flatness as in Algebra, Tags 00HB and 00DD

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$. Since the images of the $V_j$ cover $T$, there are $j$ and $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}A_j$ mapping to $\mathfrak p$. The coordinate projection $\pi_j:\prod_kA_k\to A_j$ pulls $\mathfrak q$ back to a prime of $\prod_kA_k$ whose contraction along the product map $R\to\prod_kA_k$ is $\mathfrak p$. Hence the map on spectra of the product ring map is surjective. Combining this with step 2 and the flat-plus-surjective-spectrum criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat] proves that $R\to\prod_jA_j$ is faithfully flat.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00HQ (lemma-ff-rings), equivalence of faithful flatness with surjectivity on spectra for a flat map; covering images from Topologies Definition Tag 022B
